messages:
ashley: FYI noticed a p95/p99 latency bump (~400-600ms extra) on node-gpu-12 during a 65k-token session. flame/profile points to paging in the KV arena. anyone seen this pattern?

mike: yep, saw something similar in a staging soak last week. not classic thrash — looks like sparse fragmentation + small 'holes' causing unexpected pager walks. i've been calling them "ghostholes".

sam: can you paste the profile or repro?

ashley: perf snapshot and a small trace attached below (copied output):
```
# perf top snippet
kv_pager_scan  42.3%
kv_slot_lookup 18.7%
evicter_touch  11.1%
memmove        6.2%
```
trace shows lots of short reads that end up touching multiple slabs.

perf-bot: ALERT: KV_PAGER_LATENCY spike on node-gpu-12 @ 2026-03-17T10:12Z (rule: kv-pager-90).

mike: theory: under long-context, we do a lot of incremental KV writes for prefixes. when entries are partially evicted (page-chains) they leave tiny unused ranges -> holes. our reuse/insert path then re-inserts into those gaps in a way that breaks locality, causing more page scans. LRU heuristics plus our pagination boundary math produces non-monotonic eviction order.

rachel: interesting — i dug into the kernel selection traces too: on these same requests we switched to the memory-optimized kernel because batch sequence lengths drifted; that kernel has a slightly different KV access stride which magnifies the hole problem.

sam: steps to repro (mike wrote):
```bash
# repro: stream a single conversation with rolling context + many partial prefix updates
python tools/repro_kv_holes.py --context-length 65000 --prefix-churn 1200 --concurrency 6 --duration 5m
# run with env KV_DEBUG=1 and capture /tmp/kv_pager.log
```
please run on a node with at least 2x usual heap to avoid unrelated OOMs.

ashley: ran repro on staging, confirmed p95 regression and saw repeated "hole_punch" logs with small free fragments (~128B-2KB). attaching /tmp/kv_pager.log excerpt.

mike: quick correctness note: there's an edge where FIFO eviction path will tombstone entries and then a concurrent reuse path reclaims the same slot before the LRU metadata is reconciled -> could lead to invisible double-free-like state (not memory corruption, but causes extra pager scans as we chase stale pointers).

rachel: do we have an easy mitigator? can we bias eviction to avoid reclaiming recently-touched small-fragments?

mike: short-term mitigation: bump the small-fragment coalescing threshold and delay immediate reuse for N milliseconds. config patch we've used in staging:
```yaml
kv:
  small_fragment_coalesce: 4096  # previous 1024
  reuse_delay_ms: 25
```
that dropped p95 by ~200ms in my staging runs.

sam: long-term: we should consider making the eviction handshake idempotent and add a compacting pass that consolidates adjacent tiny free ranges when GC runs. also evaluate whether the memory-optimized kernel's stride can be smoothed.

ashley: logged issue: INFRA-1289 (ghosthole fragmentation + FIFO/LRU race). assigning to @mike for the mitig and @rachel for kernel/batching correlation.

mike: I'll open a small PR with the config defaults + a test that reproduces the hole pattern in the unit harness. test will assert no "hole_punch" logs under steady commit.

rachel: i'll add a microbenchmark for the kernel stride variance and run across model sizes. if we see consistent amplification, we can flag kernel selection to prefer stride-stable kernels under high-prefix-churn.

ashley: awesome. follow-ups: 1) PR for config bump + unit test (mike) 2) kernel microbenchmark and selection proposal (rachel) 3) add repro script to perf CI so we catch regressions. i'll update INFRA-1289 with timelines. :thumbsup:

mike: noted. will also add a short-term metric to the console (kv-small-frag-rate) so we can alert before latency spikes.

sam: thanks all — tagging this one for postmortem if it reoccurs in prod.
